text:
Maya R: DeployBot just put the rollout on HOLD for release v3.7.2 — 5% slice, p95 latency +40% on /generate. Checking if this is noise or we need a manual rollback.
Arjun P: saw the alert, looks reproducible on canary. metrics/trace link: https://telemetry/redwood/trace/3.7.2/aa12
Lena S: what are the rollback criteria we should apply here? auto rules say >30% p95 increase for 2 consecutive minutes triggers hold, but do we auto-revert?
Maya R: we usually only auto-revert for error-rate spikes. Latency we prefer manual unless SLA impact. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Kai T: agree. latency-only -> manual decision. But we should prepare a quick pin & rollback playbook in case it gets worse.
DeployBot: rollout paused at 2026-03-20T15:10Z by autosignal (p95_latency 42% over baseline). Suggested actions: `notify(#eng-oncall)`, `run-eval quick-smoke`, `consider partial revert`
Ops Oncall: I'm online. I'll run the smoke now and check dedicated pools vs hosted. ETA 3m.
Lena S: quick checklist proposal: 1) confirm signal with smoke test 2) check KV cache hit rates and kvcache logs 3) if noise, continue hold and monitor 4) if confirmed across regions, prepare manual revert on 5% slice -> 0% 5) notify CS + customer-facing comms
Maya R: add step: draft short customer note if we plan revert. Keep it factual: what, when, impact, rollback ETA.
Arjun P: smoke results: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.test/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq '.latency'` — p95 locally matches production spike. KV cache miss rate also up ~12%.
Kai T: kvcache miss sounds like model hotpath change. I'm leaning to revert to v3.7.1 on the affected slice. I'll prepare the revert command and release-note blurb.
Maya R: good. CS Lead, can you prepare a 1-paragraph heads-up for customers on Dedicated capacity? Mention we're investigating latency and may do a safe rollback affecting <=5% traffic.
CS Lead: on it. Draft: "We're investigating an increase in latency for a small subset of requests on v3.7.2. We may roll back that version for affected customers to restore latency while we investigate. No data loss expected. We'll update within 30 minutes."
DeployBot: proposed revert command: `revert --service=inference --from=3.7.2 --to=3.7.1 --slice=5% --reason="p95 latency regression"`
Maya R: approve revert if Ops Oncall confirms smoke & kvcache findings. Kai, Arjun — pair on executing. Tag me when you start.
Ops Oncall: Confirmed. Executing smoke -> results consistent across canary and us-west-2. Proceeding with revert on 5% slice in 2m.
Kai T: running revert now. command: `./deployctl revert --env=prod --service=inference --target-version=3.7.1 --slice=5%`
DeployBot: revert started. will report progress.
Maya R: communications: CS Lead please post the draft to #customer-updates once revert is in progress. Also update release notes section: "rolled back v3.7.2 on small traffic slice due to latency regression; investigating root cause (kvcache/attention kernels)."
CS Lead: posted and pinged key customers.
DeployBot: revert completed on slice. metrics: p95 back to baseline within 60s. full rollout paused pending investigation.
Maya R: great. Next steps: create a short postmortem stub, tag eng-ml for kernel/quantization review, and schedule a repro run in staging with synthetic KV miss pattern. I'll own the comms follow-up.
Arjun P: filing the postmortem stub and assigning to @eng-ml. Also adding a regression test to our canary smoke for KV miss patterns.
Lena S: thanks everyone. Recording: manual rollback executed after autosignal hold for latency, criteria applied = confirmed cross-region smoke + KV miss correlation, rollback slice = 5%, customer comms sent.
Kai T: adding runbook note: if p95-only holds with KV miss >10% -> manual revert slice 5% and notify CS within 10m.
Maya R: closing thread once postmortem link is up. :thumbsup:
